gloss: a warning from the past; learn from others' mistakes
teaser: Ever wondered how the past can guide our future decisions?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how the past can guide our future decisions?[break 1s]The phrase is: 前车之鉴, qián chē zhī jiàn.[break 0.5s]前 (qián) - front; [break 0.5s]车 (chē) - vehicle; [break 0.5s]之 (zhī) - of; [break 0.5s]鉴 (jiàn) - mirror or lesson. [break 1s]The full idiom is 前车之鉴, which literally means 'the mirror of the front car,' and figuratively suggests learning from the mistakes of those who came before us.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]This idiom comes from an ancient Chinese proverb about a chariot. It refers to a situation where a previous vehicle had an accident, serving as a warning to those who follow. The lesson is clear: observe the failures of others to avoid making the same mistakes yourself.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 我们应该记住前车之鉴。 [break 1s]We should remember the lessons from past mistakes. [break 1s]Example 2: 他的失败是我们前车之鉴。 [break 1s]His failure is our lesson to learn from. [break 1s]Example 3: 这次计划要考虑前车之鉴。 [break 1s]This plan should take past mistakes into account. [break 1s]So, 前车之鉴, meaning to learn from past mistakes; thank you for listening and see you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
